summary.one_liner: AgentForge is a low-code framework for building, testing, and iterating on AI-powered autonomous agents and multi-agent cognitive architectures, configured largely through YAML.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes AgentForge as a framework where agents are defined with YAML prompt templates and configuration, and composed into workflows using declarative "Cogs" that handle branching logic and memory. Persona YAML files configure agent identity and style, and prompt templates adapt to context and memory. Memory nodes are declared in Cogs and made available to agents automatically. The README says it supports OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Anthropic Claude models, plus local models through Ollama and LMStudio, and that different agents can use different LLMs. Prompts can be edited on the fly without restarting. The README's documentation section points to a docs hub with a quickstart that scaffolds a .agentforge/ directory and a no-credential debug smoke test, and a first-run guide that defaults to a Codex OAuth model path.
use_cases: build multi-agent systems with YAML workflows
run different LLMs for different agents
add persistent contextual memory to LLM agents
run local models via Ollama or LMStudio
how_to_run: Read the AgentForge Documentation docs hub (linked in the README)
Follow the Quickstart: install, scaffold .agentforge/, run the no-credential debug smoke test
Follow the First Real Model Run guide to configure the default Codex OAuth model or another provider
stack: Python (implied by the framework; not named explicitly in the README)
notable: Declarative Cogs in YAML orchestrate multi-agent workflows, branching, and memory
Agents, prompts, and personas are configured via YAML files
Per-agent LLM selection across cloud and local providers
Prompts can be edited live without restarting the system
Docs hub with a no-credential smoke test before any real model setup
caveats: README does not state supported operating systems or minimum requirements
The README itself is mostly an overview; detailed setup lives in the external docs hub
Default real-model path uses Codex OAuth, which requires credentials for that provider
